summary: Dayong (1893–1929) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute, where he taught in 1923, and was instructed by Taixu, Paldan Tenzin Nyandrak, Bai Puren, and Dorje Geshe.

Debala Mitra (1925–2003) worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. A student of Dineschandra Sircar, she served at the Archaeological Survey of India as Additional Director General from 1981 to 1983, succeeding Bal Krishen Thapar in 1981.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak (born 1931) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He founded the Central Institute of Indian Languages, serving as Director (~1969–1989), and later chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research (~2013).

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) was an Indian philosopher and Indologist. He earned his B.A. from the University of Calcutta, where he was supervised by Surendranath Dasgupta and taught by Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, later serving at City College, Kolkata (~1943–1978).

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian and Tibetologist who earned her PhD at Harvard under Oleg Grabar and completed her Habilitation at the University of Vienna. She held the Asian art history chair at the University of Vienna (1994–2015).
Declan Quigley works in Indology and related fields. He has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei (born 1968) is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his Ph.D. at Renmin University of China (~1995–1998), where he became an associate professor of religious studies around 2002.
Demchok Dorje was a scholar who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Denis Sinor (1916–2011) specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and history. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at the University of Cambridge, later holding posts at Cambridge (1948–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett (1925–2006) was a Sinologist and historian who studied at SOAS and St Catharine's College. He held Chairs of Chinese at the University of London (1960–1968) and Cambridge (1968–1980), later serving as professor emeritus at Princeton (1980–1994).

Denise Bernot (1922–2016) was a linguist who studied at the École des chartes and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes. She spent her career teaching at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from circa 1960 to 1989.

Denma Lochö Rinpoche (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric College. He served as abbot of Namgyal Monastery (1986–1991) and principal of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (~1999–2005).

Dennis A. Johnson specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012) and worked at the university's South Asian, Tibetan and Buddhist Studies Library (attested 2022).

Dennis Genpo Merzel (born 1944) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He was educated at the University of Southern California and its Rossier School of Education, and he studied under traditional teacher Taizan Maezumi (~1972–1995).

Dennis Hirota (born 1946) specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at UC Berkeley and Nagoya University, he served at Hongwanji International Center (~1976–1990) and held professorships at Chikushi Jogakuen University (~1990–1996) and Ryukoku University (~1996–2017).

Denzaburo Yoshizawa (1924–2003) was a Japanese philosopher. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1947–1950) and later held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1953–1987) and Iryo Sosei University.

Derek F. Maher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, lectured at Virginia and UNC Greensboro, and co-directed the Religious Studies Program at East Carolina University.

Dermot Killingley (born 1935) specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Merton College, Oxford, and SOAS, he taught at the University of Malaya (1961–1968) and served as Reader at Newcastle University from 1970 to 2000.

Dermott Walsh is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He completed a BA at Trinity College Dublin (2003), an MA at Leiden University (2009), and a PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles (2018) under William M. Bodiford.

Devadatta Ramakrishna Bhandarkar (1875–1950) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as the Carmichael Professor at the University of Calcutta (attested 1910) and as Superintendent of the Western Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1917).
